family: CME/CBOT Spot-Quoted Futures ("SQF") — CME Rulebook Chapter 24 / CBOT Rulebook Chapter 24. A single product family with one published Globex clock covering both the equity-index and the cryptocurrency underliers. NOT the CME equity-index Globex family, and NOT the CME cryptocurrency family (which went 24/7 on 2026-05-29 while SQF explicitly did not).
products:
Eight tradable Globex/clearing codes, all Rulebook Chapter 24:

EQUITY INDEX (listed 2025-06-30)
- QSPX — Spot-Quoted Standard and Poor's 500 Stock Price Index Futures (commodity code QSF, CME 24, Globex security group D1, CME productId 11086)
- QNDX — Spot-Quoted Nasdaq-100 Index Futures (QNF, CME 24, group D2, id 11088)
- QRTY — Spot-Quoted Russell 2000 Index Futures (QRF, CME 24, group D3, id 11090)
- QDOW — Spot-Quoted Dow Jones Industrial Average Index Futures (QDF, CBOT 24 per SER-9506R; the live spec page shows "CME 24", group D4, id 11092)

CRYPTOCURRENCY (QBTC/QETH listed 2025-06-30; QSOL/QXRP listed 2025-12-15)
- QBTC — Spot-Quoted Bitcoin Futures (QTF, CME 24, group D5, id 11094)
- QETH — Spot-Quoted Ether Futures (QEF, CME 24, group D6, id 11096)
- QSOL — Spot-Quoted SOL Futures (QOF, CME 24, group D7, id 11415)
- QXRP — Spot-Quoted XRP Futures (QXF, CME 24, group D9, id 11417)

Not executable instruments (do not model as sessions): the cleared/"non-trade" legs QSF/QNF/QRF/QDF/QTF/QEF/QOF/QXF and the Financing-Adjustment marker codes QSM/QNM/QDM/QRM/QTM/QEM/QOM/QXM. CME's own client wiki lists these marker/non-trade codes alongside the four crypto SQF roots in its "Products Not In Scope" table.
timezone: America/Chicago. CME states SQF hours in ET in the SERs ("Unless otherwise specified, times referenced herein shall refer to and indicate Eastern Prevailing Time (EPT)" — CME Rulebook Ch. 24 §2400) and in CT on the contract-spec pages and the trading-hours service; ET and CT shift together, so the CT grid is stable year-round.

MODEL MAPPING (America/Chicago, seconds since midnight, close END-EXCLUSIVE):
- regular (RTH): EMPTY — see `unsourced`. No CME primary document classifies any part of the SQF session as Regular vs Extended.
- extended (executable, trades print): days Sun,Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu; open_ssm 61200 (17:00); close_ssm 57600 (16:00 next local day) — a midnight-wrapping rule. Friday is not an opening day, which produces the weekend close.
- order_entry (Pre-Open; book accepts/amends/cancels, matching engine not running, nothing prints):
    Sunday only: 57600 → 61200 (16:00–17:00 CT), 60 minutes.
    Mon–Thu:     60300 → 61200 (16:45–17:00 CT), 15 minutes.
- Fully closed with no queue: Mon–Thu 16:00–16:45 CT (the first 45 minutes of the 60-minute maintenance break), and Friday 16:00 CT through Sunday 16:00 CT.
- Final daily close: YES — 16:00 CT on each of Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri.
- Weekend close: YES — Friday 16:00 CT to Sunday 16:00 CT (queue) / 17:00 CT (matching).
- Trade-date convention (from the service payload): the Sunday 17:00 open and the Mon–Thu 17:00 re-opens carry the FOLLOWING business day's trading date; the 16:00 close carries the current trading date.
- CME ClearPort (Sun 17:00 – Fri 17:45 CT, no reporting Mon–Thu 17:45–18:00 CT) is a clearing-submission window, not an executable window and not a Globex queue. Do not model it as a session.

CONTRAST (same service, same week, to show these are genuinely distinct clocks):
- Bitcoin Futures BTC (group BF): 2026-09-14 preopen@16:01, open@16:02, closed@16:00 … 2026-09-19 (Sat) closed@02:00, preopen@03:45, open@04:00 — i.e. the 24/7 crypto grid. SQF crypto is NOT on this.
- E-mini S&P 500 ES (group ES): envelope currently identical to SQF at open/close/preopen granularity, but its spec page additionally publishes TACO/BTIC/TMAC sub-sessions and the crate's equity-index key carries an 08:30–15:15 CT RTH that SQF does not have.

unsourced: REGULAR vs EXTENDED classification — completely unsourced. No CME primary document splits the SQF session into RTH and ETH. SER-9506R and SER-9630RR publish exactly one 'CME Globex' line per product; all eight live contract-spec pages publish exactly one 'CME Globex' line; the SQF FAQ (https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/faqs/faq-spot-quoted-futures.html, all 20+ accordions expanded and searched) contains no occurrence of 'hours' at all; CME Rulebook Chapter 24 §2402.A and CBOT Chapter 24 §24102.A both say only 'Futures contracts shall be scheduled for trading during such hours and for delivery in such months as may be determined by the Exchange.' The whole 17:00-16:00 CT window must therefore go in `extended` with `regular` empty — the same treatment src/calendar/schedules/futures/us/cryptocurrency.rs already gives its five-day era. Assigning an 08:30-15:15 CT RTH to the four equity-index SQF roots would be an invention.

CONTINUITY OF THE PRE-OPEN BETWEEN 2025-06-30 AND TODAY — I can prove the Pre-Open at launch (SER-9506R) and today (CME trading-hours service, week of 2026-09-13), and I found no notice amending it, but no single document affirms that it never moved in between. The negative is a search result, not a statement.

NOTICE-SWEEP COVERAGE GAP — I paged CME's own notice-search JSON (https://www.cmegroup.com/content/cmegroup/en/notices/jcr:content/main-content-section/section/section-elements/search_sort_filter_d.ssfajax.<page>.0.2025-04-01.2027-03-05.json) over the window 2025-04-01 to 2027-03-05, 1821 notices in 61 pages, and read pages 0-59. Pages 60-61 (the earliest, roughly the first days of April 2025, i.e. before the family existed) were not read. Every SQF hit found: SER-9506R, clearing 25-154, clearing 25-201, MSN06-25-25, MSN11-14-25, clearing 25-348, SER-9630RR, MSN02-11-26, SER-9739. NONE of them amends trading hours.

HOLIDAY / EARLY-CLOSE GRID — not enumerated. Spot-checking the Labor Day week (2026-09-06..09-12) via the same service returned a visibly different, reduced event set (no Sunday 2026-09-06 events; Monday 2026-09-07 preopen@16:45/open@17:00 for trade date 09-08), so U.S. holiday handling for this family is real and is NOT covered by this report.

WHETHER THE FRIDAY 16:00 CT CLOSE IS 'FINAL DAILY' VS 'WEEKLY' IN CME'S OWN VOCABULARY — the service simply emits closed@16:00 on Friday with no following preopen until Sunday; CME publishes no separate label. The weekend close is inferred from the absence of Saturday events plus the SER's 'Sunday 6:00 p.m. - Friday - 5:00 p.m. ET' wording.

CME rule-filing PDFs and notice PDFs on cmegroup.com are publicly reachable without any login, but Akamai 403s plain automated clients. I retrieved them with a real browser session's bot cookies. LAW-PUBLIC-SOURCES is satisfied (no authentication anywhere), but a naive curl of these URLs will return 403 and a re-verifier should use a browser.
reuse_verdict:
NEEDS ITS OWN KEY. One key for all eight roots — do not split equity-index from crypto.

Why it cannot reuse `globex_equity_index`:
- That key carries a `regular` RTH of 08:30-15:15 CT (src/calendar/schedules/futures/us/cme_group.rs, CME_REGULAR). SQF has no published RTH at all. Pointing QSPX/QNDX/QDOW/QRTY at that key would assert an RTH split that no CME document states for these contracts.
- That key's timeline runs from the January-2010 floor with dated revisions at 2012-11-18, 2015-09-20 and 2021-06-27 (removal of the 15:15-15:30 halt), plus the disputed Sunday-queue bracket. SQF did not exist before 2025-06-30, so every one of those revisions is inapplicable and reuse would silently back-date the family by fifteen years — a direct violation of "a family's history may begin only at the first source that LISTS that family's product."
- The fact that ES and QSPX currently return an identical open/close/preopen envelope from CME's trading-hours service is exactly the "matching current envelope" the brief says must not drive the verdict.

Why it cannot reuse `globex_cryptocurrency`:
- That key moved to 24/7 effective 2026-05-29 (CME submission 26-114). CME excluded SQF from that migration by name and by instrument table. QBTC/QETH/QSOL/QXRP are still on the five-day 17:00-16:00 CT grid today, verified product-by-product against CME's own trading-hours service on 2026-09-05. Reuse would produce a market that is open all weekend when it is in fact closed from Friday 16:00 CT.

Why the equity-index and crypto SQF roots share ONE key rather than two:
- Product-family semantics, not envelope coincidence. All eight are the same instrument type in the same rulebook chapter (CME 24 / CBOT 24), created by the same product design (Spot Equivalent Quoted Price + Financing Adjustment), and CME administers them as one family: SER-9506R prints ONE identical "Trading and Clearing Hours" cell in both its equity-index exhibit and its cryptocurrency exhibit; SER-9630RR reprints that same cell for QSOL/QXRP; SER-9739 amends "the Listing Schedule of all CME and CBOT Spot-Quoted Futures" in a single table spanning all eight. There is no document in which the equity SQF grid and the crypto SQF grid differ.
- The one thing that did threaten to split them — the 2026-05-29 crypto 24/7 migration — is precisely the event CME used to keep them together: it moved the crypto family away from SQF, not the crypto SQF away from the equity SQF.
- The distinct Globex security groups (D1/D2/D3/D4 equity, D5/D6/D7/D9 crypto) are a market-data partition on MDP channel 326 / market segment 74, not a schedule difference; all eight returned identical schedules.

Launch-date handling (the one wrinkle):
- The key's history begins 2025-06-30 for QSPX, QNDX, QRTY, QDOW, QBTC, QETH. QSOL and QXRP begin 2025-12-15. That is a per-root listing date, not a family clock revision — the grid is byte-identical. Model it the way cryptocurrency.rs already models ETH/MBT/MET joining a live family in 2021 ("their individual launch dates are intentionally not family-clock revisions"), i.e. one key from 2025-06-30 with QSOL/QXRP gated by their own listing date if the crate exposes per-root listing, and closed before it otherwise. The crate's January-2010 floor is far below both dates and is not engaged.
